newsitem.title: USA: NHL-BRUINS BEAT AVALANCHE DESPITE FORSBERG'S RETURN.
newsitem.headline: NHL-BRUINS BEAT AVALANCHE DESPITE FORSBERG'S RETURN.

text.p: Rob Tallas made 20 saves and Adam Oates had a goal and an assist to pace the Boston Bruins to a 4-1 victory over the Colorado Avalanche Saturday, spoiling the return of Peter Forsberg.
Tallas made eight saves in the first period, three in the second and nine in the third to stop the league's top team.
He missed a chance at his first career shutout when Forsberg set up Eric Lacroix's goal, a slap shot from the left circle, 7:06 into the third period.
"The fans knotted it tonight," Tallas said. "They were loud and that helped us. We gave them something to cheer about."

Forsberg missed 17 games after suffering a deep thigh bruise. "I was a little tired in the second period but I got a second wind in the third," Forsberg said. "It took a little while to get adjusted to playing again."

Former Bruin Craig Billington had 21 saves starting in place of Patrick Roy, who has a sprained thumb and will be out about a week. Even with their rash of injuries, the Avalanche were 10-1-3 in their last 14 games before the loss.
Trent McCleary, Ted Donato and Ray Bourque scored the other Boston goals.
At Los Angeles, Kai Nurminen took advantage of two poor clearing attempts and scored with 2:45 left in regulation as the Kings tied the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim 2-2.
"It was like the Ducks players were passing the puck to me," he said.
The tie moved the Kings to 3-0-2 in their last five meetings with their southern California rivals.
Steve Rucchin and Sean Pronger tallied for the Ducks. Yanic Perreault got the Kings' other goal.

In Buffalo, Nelson Emerson scored twice and set up the other three goals and Sean Burke made 35 saves as the Hartford Whalers broke a nine-game road losing streak by cooling off Dominik Hasek and the Sabres 5-1.
It was the second career five-point effort for Emerson, who had gone eight games since his last goal.
Hasek surrendered five goals on only 18 shots after stopping 75-of-77 in his previous two starts.
In Montreal, Joe Murphy had a goal and three assists, Brett Hull and Jim Campbell each scored twice and ex-Canadien captain Pierre Turgeon had a pair of assists in an 8-1 rout by the St Louis Blues.
St Louis, which registered a season-high in goals, is 5-2 since Joel Quenneville took over for Mike Keenan as coach, and has won three straight.

At Florida, Scott Mellanby scored twice in a 50-second span during a three-goal second period and an apparent tying tally was disallowed late in the third, enabling the Panthers to escape with a 3-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning.
John Vanbiesbrouck made 28 saves for Florida, 1-0-1 against its intrastate rivals this season and 10-4-3 all-time.

At New York, Derek Armstrong scored the go-ahead goal with 5:22 remaining and Eric Fichaud made a career-high 47 saves as the Islanders beat the Chicago Blackhawks at home for the first time in more than 12 years, 3-2.
The Islanders tied a season high with their third straight win and improved to 2-0 under new coach Rick Bowness.
The Isles snapped a 13-game home winless streak against the Blackhawks.
In Philadelphia, Tomas Holmstrom and Brendan Shanahan scored 34 seconds apart in the first period and the Detroit Red Wings limited the Flyers to only 18 shots en route to a 4-1 victory.
Kris Draper and Steve Yzerman also tallied for the Red Wings, who won for just the second time in their last 10.
Philadelphia managed only eight shots over the first two periods and lost for just the second time in 23 games.
In Phoenix, Nikolai Khabibulin stopped 26 shots for his first shutout in nearly a year and Jeremy Roenick scored twice as the Coyotes blanked the Vancouver Canucks 4-0.
Mike Gartner added a goal and an assist for Phoenix and is two assists shy of becoming just the fifth player in NHL history with 600 goals and 600 assists.
In Pittsburgh, Mark Messier scored the tying goal and set up Adam Graves's game-winner in a 2:37 span of the third period and the New York Rangers beat the Penguins 7-4.

New York improved to 3-0 against the Penguins this season, outscoring them 23-8. The Rangers got 28 saves from Mike Richter in his return from a two-game absence with a mild shoulder sprain and are 3-1-1 in their last five.

In Toronto, Todd Harvey and Mike Modano each had a goal and an assist and Andy Moog turned aside 29 shots as the Dallas Stars surpassed their win total for all of last season with a 5-1 defeat of the Maple Leafs.
Jamie Langenbrunner added a pair of assists for the first-place Stars (27-17-4), who picked up their league-leading 16th road win.
